issues.title: Test swallows send()'s closed_error without asserting it was thrown
issues.verdictReason: The try/catch at rpc_test.cc:2016-2020 only reacts to a thrown rpc::closed_error; it does not fail if stream_send_empty_frame() instead resolves successfully, relying entirely on the later put_after_close check to catch that case.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Test does not assert send() throws closed_error on refusal

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: The try/catch around the hook passes whether send() succeeds or throws closed_error; the only assertion is !st.put_after_close, so a regression where send() silently drops the frame would still pass.

issues.title: Mid-test assertion/exception failure leaves the parked sink unclosed and aborts
issues.verdictReason: If BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL at line 2000 fails, or the hook/close throw something unexpected, release_close.set_value() at line 2026 is never reached, so test_data_sink_impl::close() (line 1890-1893) stays parked on the shared_promise and `sink` is destroyed unclosed, tripping SEASTAR_ASSERT(sink_closed()) in sink_impl::~sink_impl (rpc_impl.hh:935) and aborting the whole test binary instead of reporting a clean failure.
issues.scopeReason: The test and its close-parking fixture are new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Failed assertion or exception during test skips close-parking cleanup

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: If the BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL at :2000 fails, the hook throws something other than closed_error, or sink_closed.get() fails, the cleanup (release_close.set_value(), sink_closed.get(), server_done.get()) is skipped, leaving the connection parked until timeout or an abort in ~sink_impl.

issues.title: close_entered_cv.wait() has no timeout, so a regression hangs the suite
issues.verdictReason: condition_variable::wait() at line 2011 has no deadline; if a regression stalled before reaching data_sink::close(), the test would hang until the external test.py timeout (300s) rather than failing with a clear message.
issues.scopeReason: New test code introduced by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: close_entered_cv.wait() has no timeout

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: If a regression stalls before data_sink::close() is reached, the test hangs until test.py's 300s timeout instead of failing cleanly.

issues.title: New drain in stream_close() is untested for the race it exists to fix
issues.verdictReason: In the test, sink(1).get() (rpc_test.cc:2003) completes and is awaited before sink.close() is called, so _outgoing_queue_ready is already a ready future when stream_close() captures queue_drained at rpc.cc:562 -- the 'frame queued just before the flag was set' scenario the drain exists for is never exercised. server_factory's hooks (rpc_test.cc:1966-1970) are installed but never fired, so server-side stream connections and a close_source()-triggered stream_close() (rpc.hh:356) also have no coverage, and stream_close()'s own unbounded wait on queue_drained (no timeout or cancellation, same as the old flushing write_buf.close()) is likewise untested.
issues.scopeReason: This is the core mechanism this bug-fix PR adds; the untested interleaving is exactly the race the PR is meant to close.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Drain and server-side stream closing paths are untested; new wait in stream_close() has no timeout/cancellation described

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: The test fires the hook only after queue_drained is already ready, so the case the drain exists for (a frame queued just before the flag) is never covered; server_factory's hooks are installed but never fired, so server-side stream connections and close_source()-triggered stream_close() have no test. Separately: stream_close() now waits on _outgoing_queue_ready before closing the buffer with no timeout of its own; this is not described in the PR and not a regression versus the old flushing write_buf.close(), but it is also untested.

issues.title: Doc says dropping an unclosed sink 'is an error', understating it aborts the process
issues.verdictReason: sink_impl::~sink_impl() (rpc_impl.hh:931-936) does SEASTAR_ASSERT(this->_con->get()->sink_closed()), which aborts the process; calling that just 'an error' reads as a catchable/recoverable condition.
issues.scopeReason: This sentence is new text added by this PR's doc commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Doc says dropping an unclosed sink 'is an error', understating it aborts the process

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: It is actually a SEASTAR_ASSERT in ~sink_impl, which aborts the process, and the doc should say so.

issues.title: Doc overstates that reading to eof or throw is the only way the source closes
issues.verdictReason: source_impl::operator() (rpc_impl.hh:940-975) only calls close_source() when stream_receive fails or returns empty bufs (eof). When _bufs is already non-empty, process_one_buffer() runs directly at line 951-953 and an exception thrown by unmarshall there propagates to the caller without ever calling close_source(); closing the client or aborting the connection also release it via abort_all_streams/abort().
issues.scopeReason: New text added by this PR's doc commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Doc claim that reading until it throws is the only way to close the source is inaccurate

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: close_source() only runs on eof or when stream_receive fails; an exception from unmarshall in process_one_buffer() does not close the source, and closing the client or aborting the connection are also other ways to release it.

issues.title: Doc overstates that stream shutdown happens only once both halves are closed
issues.verdictReason: client::abort_all_streams() / connection::abort() also shut the connection down outside the normal both-halves-closed path, and the doc's own line 48-49 already says closing the client aborts any open stream, which sits in tension with the unqualified 'only once both halves are closed' at line 115.
issues.scopeReason: New text added by this PR's doc commit.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: Closing the client (abort_all_streams), connection errors, and abort() also shut it down, and the same doc's line 49 already says so.

issues.title: Comment imprecisely implies nothing ever waits on _outgoing_queue_ready again
issues.verdictReason: stop_send_loop() at rpc.cc:225 still does when_all on _outgoing_queue_ready; it only resolves immediately because stream_close() already swapped in a fresh ready future via std::exchange at line 562. The comment's 'nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready' reads as if stop_send_loop() dropped that wait entirely rather than inheriting a pre-resolved placeholder.
issues.scopeReason: New comment added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Comment inaccurately implies nothing waits on _outgoing_queue_ready anymore

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: stop_send_loop() still does when_all on _outgoing_queue_ready and _sink_closed_future; it only works because it gets the ready placeholder from std::exchange, which the comment should state instead of claiming nothing waits on it.

issues.title: ignore_ready_future() drops a failed queue-drain without logging
issues.verdictReason: This mirrors the pre-existing ignore_ready_future() on the same future chain in stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:228), done for the identical reason -- the failure was already delivered to the failing entry's own caller. It is consistent, intentional, unlogged-by-convention behavior, not a new defect this PR introduces.
issues.scopeReason: The unlogged-ignore pattern already exists elsewhere in this file; this call site just follows the established convention rather than introducing new behavior.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: ignore_ready_future() silently drops a failed queue entry without logging

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: The failure was already delivered to that entry's caller or the connection was aborted, so this is acceptable, but a debug log would help diagnosis.

issues.title: PR body doesn't explain the same unflushed frame it says it saw on the parent client
issues.verdictReason: The PR body states the core dump showed the same unflushed compressor frame on both the stream connection and its parent client, but only explains and fixes the stream-connection race. Normal (non-stream) connections only close write_buf inside stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:198-233), after _error is already set, so they don't appear to share this exact window; the PR leaves open whether the parent-client occurrence is a distinct bug, a side effect of the process aborting, or something else.
issues.scopeReason: The claim and the gap in explaining it are both in this PR's own description.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: The PR body says the same unflushed-frame issue was found on the parent client, but the fix only covers stream connections and the PR does not explain the parent-side frame.

issues.title: PR body's debug-build validation claims aren't backed by a CI link or log

Both failures are pre-existing environment/toolchain issues unrelated to files this PR touches. The claim itself is plausible from reading the code but is not independently confirmed in this environment.
issues.scopeReason: The unverified claim is made in this PR's own description.

issues.title: Fixed 10-yield polling loop is an arbitrary, non-deterministic bound
issues.verdictReason: The `for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) yield().get();` loop at line 2022-2024 has no guarantee of crossing a given reactor poll; a signal set from inside put() would make the wait for the batch flush poller deterministic instead of heuristic.

issues.title: Pass-through compressor claimed to duplicate an existing one in the file
issues.verdictReason: test_compressor_empty_frames' tracker::factory::compressor (rpc_test.cc:1729-1787) is not a plain pass-through: it prepends a metadata byte/value to every frame and runs a progress fiber to inject empty frames on demand. hook_capturing_compressor_factory's compressor only needs a transparent delegate to lz4_fragmented_compressor so the test can capture the raw send_empty_frame hook; the two serve different needs and the new one isn't a redundant copy.
issues.scopeReason: No duplication exists: the two compressors have materially different behavior for different test purposes.

issues.title: PR body overstates that the drain's wait mirrors send()'s error handling
issues.verdictReason: send() chains new entries onto _outgoing_queue_ready and propagates failures through the resulting future (rpc.cc:325-340), while stream_close()'s drain uses then_wrapped and explicitly ignore_ready_future()s a failed chain before unconditionally closing the write buffer (rpc.cc:565-569) -- a materially different error-handling shape than 'the way send() does', even though the in-code comment at rpc.cc:566-567 describes the actual behavior correctly.
issues.scopeReason: The imprecise comparison is in this PR's own description.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: PR body loosely compares the drain's wait to send(), but they differ

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: The PR says the drain waits on _outgoing_queue_ready 'the way send() does', but unlike send() it uses then_wrapped and ignores a failed chain; the code comment at rpc.cc:566 describes this correctly.
